The purpose of the TOM is to adjust the orientation of the thruster to precisely align the direction of the force to the centre of mass of the Spacecraft in order to avoid generating disturbance torques when the Hall Effect Thruster is thrusting. This will allow for uncertainties in the position of the spacecraft centre of mass as the Xenon propellant is depleted during orbit raising.
The TOM satisfies three main functions, which are to support the HET, to deploy and drive the thruster position, and to provide the necessary functional links between the HET, xenon flow controller and the spacecraft.
The TOM enables a controlled angular movement of the HET about two orthogonal and independent axes. This commanded position is then held for thruster firing with the TOM actuators in an unpowered mode without back driving. Position control can be by step counting (if stepper motors are used), and absolute position sensors as well as physical end stops are needed
The procurement of the TOM will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements”. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

-	The modernisation of the image of the Guiana Space Centre (CSG),
-	The improvement of a global tourism offer of the CSG and the expectations regarding the welcoming of visitors,
-	A strong demand for information about the CSG and space activity in French Guiana.

This information concerns the contracts for works related to museum displays, scenography and graphic aspects.
The work for the CNES/CSG, at the site of the Space Museum at the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou (French Guiana), falls within a demanding operational context (project integrating an architectural and a scenographic component, CSG environment, location), which the contractor will need to take into account in their bid.
Please note that the renovation project is also the subject of a BIM-GEM (Building Information Modelling - Management-Operation-Maintenance) strategy from the design stage through to the use of the structure
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months. These activities are part of the renovation of the Space Museum.

Work to be carried out will include:

-	Supply and installation of lighting: technical studies, supply, preparation, programming, transport and on-site installation of scenographic lighting equipment, adjustments and tests (correct operation check, regular operational testing);
